verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own bot protection: ML-based bot detection, multi-account protection, disposable-email blocking and hourly sign-up limits. It also documents built-in brute-force prevention for email/SMS one-time passcodes. Credential-stuffing defense and brute-force lockout for password sign-ins are not evidenced, and all support is vendor marketing rather than in-depth docs. Missing for 10: documented credential-stuffing protection (e.g. breached-password detection), password brute-force lockout or rate limiting, in-depth configuration docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can rely on built-in protection against bots, credential stuffing, and brute-force attacks on the auth flows

citations.quote: Bot Detection — Dramatically reduce fraudulent sign-ups with built-in, continually updated machine learning
Fast and reliable one-time passcode delivery with built-in brute force prevention.
Clerk deploys advanced bot and multi-account protection to detect and neutralize attacks in real time.
Set hourly sign-up limits per email domain and from shared infrastructure.
